name: Andraste

attributes.attribute: invoked her in a sacred rite before battle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Andraste is a British goddess. Her name means “invincibility.” The warrior queen Boudicca of the Iceni summoned her in a sacred grove before leading her troops against the Roman invaders. In the rite Boudicca set free a hare. The hare was an occasional symbol of the warrior queen Medb, famed in Ireland. At first the hare appears a small creature for a war goddess, but it turns fierce when caught, and so it fits an image of defense. Boudicca came close to driving the Romans from her land. When the war turned against her, she died by her own hand rather than face the humiliations the Romans gave their defeated enemies.
objective: Record Andraste, the British goddess of victory.
